answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down and return the rest unseen; place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories; randomly choose a structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: “randomly select number of players + 1”; “one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories”; “Randomly choose one structure bonus tile”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: On the map: each character starts at its home base, and two workers start one each on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it. On mats: four mechs over their Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat; one-time recruit spaces empty. Faction Mat provides starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat provides starting popularity, coins, and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 list mat assignments and all starting pieces.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs; top action must precede bottom if taking both. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before an action; benefits are exposed green boxes, and you may take as much or as little as desired. Exact costs/benefits are determined by the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “must move the token”; “first pay the full cost”; “choose as much or as little”; “bottom first is not allowed.”

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control section: “An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it”; “Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities”; “any territories you currently control.”

answers.answer: No: normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each, and cannot move the same unit twice. A carried worker can later move itself or be carried by a subsequent move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry any number of your workers, and never your character.
answers.evidence: Move: “two different units”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; carried worker may “subsequently move itself”; only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech entering enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers.
answers.evidence: Move: entering enemy workers only forces retreat and “stops”; a worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, combat occurs before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Combat: “After all units finish a Move action”; “attacker chooses the order”; Move: worker cannot independently move “into or out of” enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power OR one combat card; if the draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources OR one popularity. Put traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all workers are home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade action descriptions state costs, choices, deck exhaustion, resource placement, worker condition, and building bonuses.

answers.answer: First pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed during production change only future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: “Pay every exposed Produce cost ... in full before production”; new workers “left to right”; “future Produce actions.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes, as modified by mat/upgrades. Upgrade moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy puts a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability then applies to your character and all your mechs, not workers. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and the paragraph permitting payment after completing all pieces.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory containing your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases forbidden, and only one structure total per territory. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill's bonus production territory and its own production operate only while controlled; an enemy unit there removes your control and the Mill cannot produce, though it remains on the board. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled, and your units may move to/from it subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions; opponents cannot use its ability.
answers.evidence: Build description: controlled territory with worker; structures “cannot be moved or destroyed”; Mill works “only while controlled”; Mine is personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain that space's choice: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is set by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. For a triggered bottom-row action, resolve active player first, then immediate left, then immediate right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game; in two-player play the opponent triggers once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs specify placement, one-time choices, source-circle bonus, resolution order, and two-player rule.

answers.answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly chooses dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (plus one total card for Rusviet People's Army if any workers are present). If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal totals simultaneously; add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Both pay the selected dial power from their Power Track and discard all played cards face-up; card values do not reduce track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4 specify secret simultaneous choice, card cap, ability order, reveal/ties, and payment.

answers.answer: Winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (ordinarily up to two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving resources behind; Nordic Seaworthy can instead send eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie's stated combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6 state retreats, resources, popularity loss, stars, and loser's card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains there; on contested entry lost in combat, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay no normal action costs and receive no mat benefits, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after “all combats”; if contested entry is lost, “the token stays”; gains go to “the encounter territory”; no normal costs or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character takes one Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed): inspect available cards, choose one, and return the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visitors cannot exchange it. A Factory card acts as a fifth section with optional top then bottom under the normal no-repeat rule, except Rusviet. Similar Factory actions grant no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a Speed character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.
answers.evidence: Factory paragraph specifies each player's first visit, permanence, action section, excluded bonuses, and bottom Move distance.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; all requirements must be met at reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony may retain the second card after the first and score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph states timing, requirements, discards, and Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars, except Saxony), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except combat's two stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops, and another player's star does not block the goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists the achievements, persistence, non-blocking, and immediate end.

answers.answer: For a bottom-row action earning the sixth star, collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. Pending unresolved battle units are undone by returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For a neighbor's recruit star/bonus, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for the sixth star each time; once the sixth star is placed, later neighbor stars/bonuses do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence specifies bottom-action collections, pending battle undo, and active/left/right resolution.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per counted territory, and $2 per complete resource pair. Thus five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as seven (4 + 3), adding $21; 13 resources make six pairs, adding $12. These add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus. Structure bonus is earned even if enemies control your structure territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and Factory count; “earn it even if enemies control your structures' territories”; tie order listed.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, except setup, forced retreats, and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control section: “A home base is not a territory”; default entry restriction and exceptions; unmatched bases are inactive.

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village a worker. Lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources section says workers are not resources and “no supply limit.”

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources mid-movement; a mech may also carry your workers, but no mech may carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one step, with the extra step usable before or after; mechs may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move bullets on carrying, Speed, tunnel steps, and stop overrides.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit can enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: “Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure”; “All printed tunnel territories are adjacent ... by any unit.”

answers.answer: You may not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move the token to a different section and take neither action (a dead turn).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Never pay only part of a cost”; “take a dead turn by moving the token to a different section and taking neither action.”

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These bonuses trigger when taking the corresponding top action. You retain structure abilities even without control, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take the benefits away; exception: Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade bonuses and control rules on structure abilities; Mill exception.

answers.answer: Riverwalk applies to character and mechs. Rusviet: farms and villages; Crimea: farms and tundra; Nordic: forests and mountains; Polania: villages and mountains; Saxony: forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is available from the start to workers alone, allowing them to cross rivers to any land terrain but not lakes; it does not help character/mechs and gives no lake movement.
answers.evidence: Faction Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim description.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township specify locations and character/mechs.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets you pay one power before combat to reduce opponent power by two, once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Disarm and Artillery descriptions specify trigger, timing, cost/effect, and frequency.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total under People's Army (one per participating character/mech plus one additional total card when any workers are present). Workers alone never fight; at least a character/mech is required.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: “one additional combat card total”; “still requiring a character/mech”; example says two mechs and three workers allow three cards.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare row specifies destinations and excludes an active opponent's base.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of its value, once per turn.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and starting Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and between any lake and any other lake, but Polania has no Nordic adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off; carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Seaworthy/Submerge descriptions and lake note state movement, retreat distinction, and carried-piece restriction.

answers.answer: Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not cover loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description explicitly distinguishes combat from undefended workers.

answers.answer: Polania Meander permits choosing up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first option's gain can pay the second option's cost. The summary does not state that this permits drawing or using two encounter cards; it describes two options on one card.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: “up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.”

answers.answer: A character entering an encounter during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounters paragraph says this applies during Factory Move and resolves after all combats; entry forces a stop.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but card contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value when asked.
answers.evidence: Setup information paragraph: public combat-card count, secret contents/objectives, and no requirement to reveal coin total.

answers.answer: Players may make informal unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). Negotiation or payment cannot cancel combat after units have moved onto opposing units and combat is initiated; bribes may still influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph states agreements are unenforceable, coin exchange limits, and combat cannot be canceled.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, payouts are $3 per star, $2 per counted territory, $1 per complete pair of resources. At 7–12: $4, $3, $2 respectively. At 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score, so a leftover single token scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and scoring text: controlled lakes count, home bases do not, odd leftover ignored.

answers.answer: For adjacency tiles, count each qualifying feature once across all structures. Adjacent tunnels count unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; adjacent encounters count unique printed encounter locations even after the token is removed; adjacent lakes count unique lakes. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payouts by count: 1 = $2; 2–3 = $4; 4–5 = $6; tunnels at 6 = $9; lakes and encounters at 6–7 = $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table defines unique features, Mine/removed-token treatment, and thresholds; rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 = $2, 2 = $4, 3–4 = $6. Structures in a row score only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line: 1 = $2, 2 = $4, 3 = $6, 4 = $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1 = $2, 2 = $4, 3 = $6, 4 = $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table lists each count and payout; rows remain continuous across rivers.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake (unless Polania Camaraderie's applicable exception applies).
answers.evidence: Combat: popularity loss applies “even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.”

answers.answer: No. A placed popularity star is permanent, but current popularity may later drop and current popularity determines final scoring. Another player's star does not block the same goal, so both factions may earn a star for it.
answers.evidence: Stars: permanent even if popularity drops; “Other players' stars never block a goal”; current popularity determines scoring.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses may trigger for the active player and their immediate left and right neighbors.
answers.evidence: Setup mat assignment and seating steps; Ongoing recruits specifies immediate neighbors.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Movement section defines river/lake and entry “from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.”

answers.answer: No, the encounter card is not private: show it to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Show the encounter card to all players”; show artwork and read capitalized thematic text aloud.

answers.answer: There is no limit to the number of friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control section: “No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.”

answers.answer: Once the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain. The current player's interactive bonuses and game-end priority still resolve in order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, during the listed choice.

answers.answer: No. You may take a section's top action once and bottom action once in that turn; you cannot repeat either action. The exception is Rusviet's ability to repeat a section from the prior turn, including its Factory card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says each top/bottom action once and Rusviet may repeat a section.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal unupgraded Move top action.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “Alternatively gain $1.”

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. This includes workers that retreat; they retreat to their home base. The summary does not describe a way to put a board worker back on the mat to reuse a Produce cost space.
answers.evidence: Produce: “Workers never return to the Player Mat”; retreat rules send them to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both; the summary places no prerequisite on either value.
answers.evidence: Combat: “You may attack with zero power/popularity.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary limit is two combat stars, but further combats remain allowed.
answers.evidence: Combat: “You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.”

answers.answer: For a faction without Meander, you must choose one affordable option; you cannot decline to choose. An unaffordable coin/popularity option cannot be selected. You must pay the printed cost but may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters paragraph states one affordable option is mandatory, unaffordable options excluded, and benefits may be limited.

answers.answer: No turn-order selection is specified: combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly. They reveal simultaneously after optional combat cards are added.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: “simultaneously and secretly choose”; “Reveal simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.”

answers.answer: No. A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved, and placing the sixth ends play immediately. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but when revealed you must meet all requirements at that moment; it must be on your own turn before or after a top/bottom action.
answers.evidence: Stars: “Place a star as soon as you achieve”; Objectives: “You may wait” to reveal completed objective.

answers.answer: No. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: “Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.”

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on the chosen one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: the recruit “put it permanently” on a bonus; “It cannot later move.”

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Only a character triggers an encounter.”

answers.answer: While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus production territory to the current allowance: normally up to three instead of two; if the allowance was upgraded to three, up to four. The Mill counts as one producing worker even with no actual worker there, producing the terrain's normal token. Actual workers on that territory each also produce normally, so their output is added to the Mill's rather than replaced by it.
answers.evidence: Mill description: bonus territory; “Mill itself counts as one producing worker”; actual workers also produce; allowance examples.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not maintain control: after your last unit leaves a territory with no structure, you no longer control it.
answers.evidence: Control section defines control by unit or uncontested structure; resources are not listed as a basis of control.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Upgrade — oil,” “Deploy — metal,” “Build — wood,” “Enlist — food.”
